### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
Here is an example of HTML and CSS that uses flexbox to display a list of links in a condensed form:

HTML:
```
<div class="container">
  <div class="link-container">
    <a href="#" class="link">Link 1</a>
    <a href="#" class="link">Link 2</a>
    <a href="#" class="link">Link 3</a>
    <!-- Add more links here -->
  </div>
</div>
```
CSS:
```
.container {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
}

.link-container {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  justify-content: space-between;
}

.link {
  flex-basis: 30%;
  margin: 5px;
  text-align: center;
}
```
This will create a container that uses flexbox to display the links in a row, wrapping them to the next line as needed, and using `justify-content: space-between;` to distribute the links evenly across the row. Each link will take up 30% of the available space, and have a 5px margin around it.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->
